jeff: heads up — canary dashboards are showing sparkline stutter and interactive lag after the client patch rolled at 09:12. reproduced on chrome + safari. https://perf.redwood.example/ci/3421 :eyes:
maya: ugh saw that too. looks like the client sourcemap flush landed with the telemetry collector change. might be invalidating some in-memory cache
ricardo: details — what do you mean by 'sourcemap flush'? we just upload a new sourcemap to S3 and send an invalidate event to CDN. nothing should touch kv-cache right?
jeff: the CDN invalidation is fine. but the new telemetry agent added a short-lived header that forces client-side cache-busting for script bundles (Cache-Control: no-cache) during canary window. that appears to trigger module re-evaluation and memory churn in the console host leading to GC pauses
maya: exact symptoms: sparklines freeze for ~200-800ms on hover, small jank on pan. flamegraphs show main thread spikes in parsing/eval, not network.
carla: can you paste a small perf trace?
jeff: here — snippet from chrome trace (trimmed):
```
Main Thread:
 - V8 ParseModule (120ms)
 - EvaluateScript (85ms)
 - React render (45ms)
 - Layout/paint (30ms)
```

ricardo: hmm evals that long are consistent with full bundle re-download + module init. if the bundle cache is bypassed we lose pre-warmed modules and cached wasm/kernels for chart lib.
dan: is this the same as the kv-cache revalidation problem we fixed in the backend last month? sounds similar but the trigger is different (client header vs backend TTL)
maya: agree different trigger. quick mitigation: switch canary to use the prior telemetry collector (rollback header) and re-run. can we patch canary routing policy to stick to cached bundle variant?
ops-bot: canary-rollout: update request accepted — canary scope set to 5% -> 0% for build 2026.3. re-routing in 2min.
carla: long term, we should avoid adding cache-control changes during canary spikes. maybe use an explicit cache-bust query param for dev sourcemaps instead of header change. Also add a sentinel to telemetry to avoid touching asset headers
ricardo: would be good to add a small unit in runtime that detects module re-eval churn and emits telemetry (counts of EvaluateScript > 50ms). that would help alert before UX regressions.
maya: ticket created: PLAT-1137 "detect client module re-eval churn + protect canary bundles" and assigned to eng-runtime.
jeff: rolling rollback confirmed — canary latency back to baseline within 3m. leaving the thread for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
